title: Hoboken hardship rental increase requires Board approval
requirement: A landlord may not impose any rent increase under Article II without Board approval. For a hardship increase, the landlord must serve each tenant notice of the appeal at least 20 days before the hearing and show it is not earning a fair return.
coverage_conditions: Rent increases imposed on any tenant under Article II of the Hoboken rent leveling and stabilization chapter; newly constructed dwellings and buildings vacant since January 1, 1984 may be exempt.

conditions.text: newly constructed dwellings eligible for exemption
buildings completely vacant since January 1, 1984 eligible for exemption

coverage_quotes: The Regulation Officer shall make all determinations regarding the eligibility of a newly constructed dwelling for an exemption as defined above.
The Rent Regulation Officer shall make all determinations regarding the eligibility of a building completely vacant since January 1, 1984, for an exemption as defined above.

exemptions: Newly constructed dwellings and buildings completely vacant since January 1, 1984, whose eligibility for exemption is determined by the Regulation Officer and the Rent Regulation Officer (§ 155-16).
quoted_span: No landlord shall impose upon any tenant an increase in rent under this Article without first obtaining approval with the Board.

title: Hoboken capital improvement surcharge tenant notice
requirement: After the Board approves a capital improvement surcharge application, the landlord must personally serve tenants a standardized notice explaining the surcharge, base rent, apportioned surcharge, effective date and termination, and total rent, and file it with the Board and the Officer.
coverage_conditions: Landlords granted a capital improvement surcharge by the Board for dwellings under Article II of the Hoboken rent leveling chapter; newly constructed dwellings and buildings vacant since January 1, 1984 may be exempt.
